summary.text: In-Q-Tel (IQT) is a not-for-profit strategic investment firm set up by the CIA in 1999. It describes itself as independent and not part of the CIA, and it works with U.S. government partners including the CIA, NGA, FBI, NSA and DHS. Fortune reported that it receives roughly $100 million a year in taxpayer money. Its investments have included Keyhole, whose technology became Google Earth after Google acquired the company, as well as Palantir and the social-media monitoring firm Dataminr.

facts.claim: On September 29, 1999, the CIA announced the launch of In-Q-It, Inc. (later renamed In-Q-Tel), with the backing of CIA Director George Tenet. The release described it as a private, independent, non-profit corporation that would partner with information-technology companies and academia on projects of mutual interest to the CIA and the commercial marketplace.

facts.claim: In-Q-Tel invested about $2 million in Palantir Technologies early in the company's life. Forbes reported that the money was part of an initial roughly $12 million funding round led by Peter Thiel's Founders Fund.
